summary: Compared low-latency causal SC/PPG candidates and removed the measured live VisPy timebase hold by retiming committed sweep geometry instead of replaying full history. Added a correlated EEG retiming regression; native synthetic benchmark remained near 30 Hz through timebase changes.

intervals.description: Inspect current reducer implementation and compare primary literature for online low-latency SC and PPG alternatives; exact end time was not captured and is bounded at the first observed timestamp of the resumed rendering work.
evidence: Repository state checked in the user-designated local checkout

intervals.description: Diagnose unresolved EEG rendering report and timebase hold, implement immediate VisPy sweep retiming, add correlated EEG regression, and benchmark native switches.
evidence: Codex turn 2026-11-05; first observed native benchmark timestamp 16:58:43+01:00
Focused unittest runs: 23 core and 29 GUI tests

results: Native baseline reproduced the hold: first new EEG timebase draw 462 ms after switch; maximum draw gap 417 ms for the 10 s transition.

After retiming: all four EEG transitions (10, 30, 5, 15 s) drew at the new timebase within 18–23 ms; maximum draw gaps were 45–52 ms. Switch action took 6–10 ms. Benchmark used synthetic live streams with 8 displayed EEG channels.
23 core rendering tests and 29 offscreen GUI rendering tests passed; git diff --check passed.

Filter literature comparison: real-time EDA model-based Kalman filtering is a plausible causal SC candidate; PPG adaptive noise cancellation generally needs a synchronized motion reference such as accelerometry and should not be treated as a single-channel waveform filter.
Inspected the supplied Registrazione 2026-11-05 155756.mp4 in VLC; the clip shows continuous EEG traces at an 8 s window but no clear before/after timebase transition.
open_items: User should confirm the EEG appearance on the original recording or live acquisition; this session validated correlated synthetic EEG, not the specific user recording.
Select and validate SC/PPG preprocessing replacements against the GUI latency and signal-quality requirements before implementation.
limitations: The end timestamp for the earlier filter-research interval was not logged; it is bounded at the first observed timestamp for this resumed rendering work, so its duration may be overstated.
Native benchmark used synthetic streams and the current PC/driver; it does not prove behavior on every EEG device or GPU.
Offscreen GUI tests warn that QOpenGLWidget context is unavailable; native benchmark supplies the timing verification.

The supplied recording did not visibly capture the timebase change, so the native benchmark verifies switch latency while the clip cannot confirm the retiming behavior on the user's exact interaction.
